sentences.text: As per the prosecution, on 07.06.2022 a report was made at the Police Station by the informant Lalit Hardia to the effect that the deceased Asha Patel was residing in her house for about one and a half years as a tenant and was studying for UPSC.
Her relatives Surendra and the applicant were also residing in the house as tenants.
At about 1:30 p.m. when he had gone to the room of the deceased, the same was not opened despite been knocked upon.
Eventually, the door was broken and the deceased was found hanging from ceiling of the room and had committed suicide.

On the report, marg was registered and investigation was commenced during the course of which statements of witnesses were recorded and a suicide note was recovered from the body of the deceased in which she had stated that it is the present applicant, who is responsible for her death and who has taken undue advantage of her mentally as well as physically on the pretext of teaching her.
The applicant used to say that he would marry her and when she got extremely troubled, he has left her.
On the basis of the investigation conducted, the applicant has been implicated and arrested for the present offence.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case.
As many as seven witnesses have been examined before the trial Court and none of them have supported the prosecution case and have been declared hostile.

Priyanka Patel,
Pushpendra Kumar Patel and Surendra Singh Patel who are also stated to have been residing in the house, where the deceased was living have not supported the story of the prosecution.
There is no other material witness remaining to be examined on part of the prosecution.
It is further submitted that the suicide note of the deceased is ambiguous in nature and from the same, it cannot be held that it is the applicant alone who is responsible for her death.
The applicant and the deceased were in a relationship and when the same went bad, the deceased committed suicide by implicating the applicant.
There is no legal evidence of the applicant taking undue advantage of the deceased.
The applicant is in custody since 09.06.2022 and the trial is still likely to take time for its conclusion.
On such grounds prayer for grant of bail to the applicant has been made.

5. The aforesaid prayer has been opposed by the learned counsel for the respondent/State submitting that in view of the allegations levelled against the applicant, he is not entitled to be released on bail merely on the basis of statements of witnesses recorded before the trial Court.
6. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and have perused the case diary as well as the statements of witnesses.

7. Subsequent to withdrawal of the previous application, the witnesses including those who were residing in the same house as that of the deceased have been examined before the trial Court and none of them have supported the prosecution case in any manner and have been declared hostile.
Now, there does not appear to be any material witness remaining to be examined on part of the prosecution.

The suicide note recovered from the deceased does not give any specific particulars as regards the manner in which the applicant took undue advantage of her and the reason as to why he would be responsible for her death.
The applicant is in custody since 09.06.2022 and the trial is still likely to take time for its conclusion.
Thus in my opinion, the applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail.

sentences.text: Accordingly, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application filed by the applicant is allowed.

The applicant is directed to be released on bail upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the Court concerned during trial and shall also abide by the conditions enumerated under Section 437 (3) Criminal Procedure Code, 1973.
9. This order shall be effective till the end of the trial, however, in case of bail jump, it shall become ineffective.
